assessment_definition.answering_window: Typical pattern over previous 14–28 days unless an item specifies a weekly target.
assessment_definition.baseline_flow: 6 safety gates + goal/context + 36 core + 0–12 adaptive deep-dive
assessment_definition.week12_flow: 36 core by default; optional coach-enabled deep-dive after score snapshot
assessment_definition.boundary: Coaching and whole-person reflection instrument; not a medical, psychiatric, psychometric, pastoral, or spiritual diagnostic test.

questions.statement: Most of my meals are built mainly from minimally processed foods rather than packaged convenience foods.
I usually protect enough time in bed to obtain at least about 7 hours of sleep, unless a qualified professional has advised otherwise for my situation.
In a typical week I achieve at least about 150 minutes of moderate-intensity activity (or an equivalent amount of vigorous activity), when medically appropriate.
I have enough physical energy for the responsibilities that matter most to me on most days.
I regularly eat vegetables, fruit, legumes/beans, whole grains, nuts/seeds, or other fibre-rich plant foods that fit my needs and tolerances.
My bedtime and wake time are reasonably consistent across most days of the week.
I perform muscle-strengthening exercise for the major muscle groups on at least two days in a typical week, when medically appropriate.
My energy is reasonably stable rather than repeatedly swinging between pushing hard and crashing.
My main meals have enough structure and nourishment that I am not routinely driven into impulsive eating by extreme hunger.
I usually wake feeling sufficiently restored to begin the day.
I move my body on most days instead of concentrating all activity into one or two days.
I generally recover between training sessions and demanding days.
Sugary drinks, sweets, fast food, and highly processed snack foods are occasional rather than the foundation of my diet.
I have an evening routine that helps me transition from stimulation and work into sleep.
I regularly break up long periods of sitting with standing, walking, or other movement.
I adjust training, workload, food, and rest when my body is clearly showing signs of excessive strain.
I can make healthy food choices in normal life without needing an extreme, all-or-nothing diet.
I rarely sacrifice sleep unnecessarily for screens, work, entertainment, or poor planning.
My training is progressive enough to build capacity but appropriate enough that I can recover from it.
Persistent pain, dizziness, breathlessness, unexplained fatigue, or other physical symptoms do not regularly prevent me from functioning.
My relationship with food is generally purposeful and peaceful rather than dominated by guilt, chaos, restriction, or loss of control.
Daytime sleepiness or fatigue does not regularly impair my focus, safety, work, training, or relationships.
My current physical capacity supports ordinary work, family, ministry, and daily-life demands reasonably well.
I seek appropriate professional assessment when a physical problem is persistent, severe, unexplained, or outside the scope of coaching.
I engage with Scripture consistently enough that Biblical truth is shaping my decisions, not merely inspiring me occasionally.

questions.statement: When an unhelpful thought appears, I can notice it without automatically treating it as truth.
I can usually identify what I am feeling instead of only reacting to the feeling.
I know the few health actions that matter most right now instead of trying to change everything at once.
I have at least one person with whom I can speak honestly about my struggles and progress.
I can redirect my attention toward what matters when my mind becomes distracted or overwhelmed.
When I am stressed, angry, anxious, disappointed, or lonely, I can pause before acting impulsively.
I make specific plans for when, where, and how I will carry out important habits.

safety_gates.question: Has a qualified clinician told you to restrict exercise, fasting, weight loss, or major dietary changes?
safety_gates.if_yes: Coach review before prescribing or progressing those behaviours.

safety_gates.question: Do you currently have unexplained chest pain, fainting, severe shortness of breath, rapidly worsening symptoms, or another condition that may make exercise unsafe?
safety_gates.if_yes: Pause exercise programming and obtain appropriate medical clearance.

safety_gates.question: Are you pregnant, recently postpartum, recovering from surgery, or managing a medical condition that materially changes nutrition/training needs?
safety_gates.if_yes: Individualize and involve appropriate clinical expertise where needed.

safety_gates.question: Do you have a current or recent eating disorder, purging behaviour, severe restriction, or recurrent loss-of-control eating that needs specialist support?
safety_gates.if_yes: Do not treat this as a discipline problem; coordinate/referral to appropriately qualified care.

safety_gates.question: Are you currently in an acute mental-health crisis or do you need urgent mental-health support?
safety_gates.if_yes: Stop the normal assessment path and direct the client to appropriate local urgent/crisis or professional support.

safety_gates.question: Are you taking prescription medication or receiving active treatment that may materially affect energy, appetite, sleep, body weight, training tolerance, mood, or test results?
safety_gates.if_yes: Record for coach/clinical context; never advise medication changes.

interpretation_bands.label: Needs attention
interpretation_bands.coach_stance: A meaningful gap is present; choose high-leverage actions and clarify obstacles.

interpretation_bands.label: Building
interpretation_bands.coach_stance: Useful foundation with inconsistent areas; reinforce systems and progression.

interpretation_bands.label: Strong foundation
interpretation_bands.coach_stance: Mostly dependable; optimize only where it serves the client’s calling and goals.

interpretation_bands.label: Consistently supported
interpretation_bands.coach_stance: Do not chase perfection. Maintain, protect and redirect attention to the next meaningful constraint.

trigger_rules.assignment: domain is eligible for both deep-dive questions
domain is eligible for one deep-dive question

selection_algorithm: Build the set of triggered domains using AD1/AD2.
Sort triggered domains by core_domain_score ascending, then primary-goal relevance descending, then domain code.
Pass 1: assign the first deep-dive item from every triggered domain in sorted order until the global cap is reached.
Pass 2: for AD1 domains only, assign the second deep-dive item in the same sorted order until the global cap is reached.
Never assign more than 12 automatic deep-dive questions.
Freeze the assignment set when the client enters Adaptive Deep Dive. If core answers are edited afterward, require explicit regeneration and preserve an audit event.
adaptive_deep_dive.scoring_rule: Deep-dive and coach-clarification responses never contribute to domain, pillar, or KCI scores in v2.
adaptive_deep_dive.reassessment_rule: Week-12 reassessment repeats the 36 Core questions only by default. Adaptive follow-up may be coach-enabled after the comparison snapshot, but it never changes the comparison scores.

scoring.pillar_formula: arithmetic mean of four core-domain scores
scoring.kci_formula: arithmetic mean of Body, Soul, Spirit pillar scores
scoring.missing_core_rule: No score or submission until all 36 core items are answered, unless a coach-approved exemption exists.
scoring.exemption_rule: If a coach-approved exemption removes one core item from a domain, normalize to remaining maximum. Require at least 2 scored core items; otherwise domain=insufficient_data and suppress pillar/KCI completeness.

energy_capacity.label: More usable energy and physical capacity

food_freedom.label: Reduce food chaos, guilt or loss-of-control patterns

stress_resilience.label: Build emotional resilience and healthier stress responses

purpose_calling.label: Clarify purpose and build capacity for calling

leverage_rules.reason: Sleep/recovery is low while energy, focus or emotional resilience is also low.
Follow-through is low while multiple other domains need attention; implementation may constrain progress across the plan.
Nutrition structure is low alongside physical readiness or follow-through.
Stress/emotional regulation is low alongside nutrition, sleep or follow-through.
Movement/strength is low alongside physical readiness or follow-through.
Support/environment is low alongside follow-through or community/calling.
Stewardship/self-control is low alongside follow-through or nutrition structure.
Calling/community is low alongside support or usable physical capacity.

big3.readiness: 0–10; domain readiness else general readiness else 5
big3.client_publication: Big 3 remain hidden until coach approval.

spirit_score_disclaimer: Spirit scores reflect reported rhythms and alignment in the constructs measured here. They do not measure salvation, holiness, spiritual maturity, God’s approval, or a person’s worth.
